annotation.title_clean: Is It Time to Consider EU Criminal Law Rules on Robotics?
annotation.title_en: Is It Time to Consider EU Criminal Law Rules on Robotics?
annotation.venue: Croatian Yearbook of European Law and Policy
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Journal article asking whether the EU should develop criminal law rules for AI and robots. It reviews EU AI regulatory action, including the Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI, and examines AI in criminal proceedings and AI as a potential perpetrator. It argues the EU should regulate criminal liability for AI acts, calling this a "third revolution" in criminal law.
key_provisions_or_claims: EU legislator should consider a framework of criminal law rules for AI use.
AI use in criminal investigation and proceedings (e.g., neuro-interrogation) merits EU-level principles and standards.
Criminal liability for acts of AI (traffic, weapons, medicine) is unresolved in current criminal law.
Criminal liability of AI is not yet accepted nor conceivable in modern criminal law.
Criminal liability for AI acts is the 'third revolution' of criminal law; the EU should act in a timely manner.
